''Escallonia montevidensis'' (Cham. & Schltdl.) DC. }} '''''Escallonia bifida''''', the '''cloven gum box''', is an [[evergreen]] shrub or small tree in the family [[Escalloniaceae]]. It is native to [[Brazil]] and [[Uruguay]].{{NSW Flora Online|author= |genus=Escallonia |species=bifida|accessdate=24 March 2014 }} It can grow up to {{convert|4 |m|ft|abbr=on}} high and {{convert|2.5 |m|ft|abbr=on}} broad, and has dark green shiny leaves which are 2 to 7 cm long and 0.8 to 2 cm wide. The pure white flowers, initially tubular but then spreading, appear in summer. It is sparingly naturalised in [[New South Wales]] in Australia. It is found in cultivation in mild coastal regions of the [[UK]] (hardy down to {{convert|-5 |C|F|abbr=on}}, where its dense habit makes it suitable for tall hedging. In colder areas it requires the protection of a wall. It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/44649/i-Escallonia-bifida-i/Details | title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Escallonia bifida'' | access-date=16 February 2018}}{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 37 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 19 February 2018}} The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''bifida'' means "cleft in two".{{cite book |last=Harrison |first=Lorraine |title=RHS Latin for Gardeners |year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley |location=United Kingdom |isbn=978-1845337315 }} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q16981770}} [[Category:Escallonia|bifida]] [[Category:Flora of Brazil]] [[Category:Flora of Uruguay]] [[Category:Flora naturalised in Australia]] {{Asterid-stub}}
